1.name: Trey McBride
1.comment: McBride had one of the best seasons ever for a tight end last year. He had numbers of an elite No. 1 receiver at the tight end position. He was first overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He had 126 receptions for 1,239 yards and 11 touchdowns. He had a huge turnaround in the touchdown department, taking his fantasy game to a new level. McBride had double-digit fantasy points all but two games. He had 20-plus points seven times. McBride was a clear difference-maker for fantasy teams, He has two straight seasons with 100-plus receptions and 1,100-plus yards. He might be the best tight end in football right now and will continue to be the top target in the Cardinals offense. McBride is a well-rounded tight end, doing well as a receiver and blocker. He is very good at making plays after the catch. He also has great hands and his route running continues to get better and better.
1.outlook: Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride put together a phenomenal 2025 season, ranking as the overall TE1 in PPR leagues with 126 catches, 1,239 yards, and 11 touchdowns. He was at his best when the Cardinals had Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. In his five weeks with Kyler Murray, he averaged 12.5 fantasy points and ranked as the TE4. That's not bad by any means, but it's significantly inferior to his production through 12 weeks with Brissett, when he averaged 21.1 points per game. During that span, he was the undisputed TE1, scoring a whopping 90 points more than the TE2 (Kyle Pitts). Brissett has already held himself out of some practices due to a contract issue, but assuming he's named the starter for 2026, we would expect McBride to be the odds-on favorite to finish as the overall TE1 for a second year in a row. He's a target machine who is capable of making athletic plays downfield, breaking tackles, and scoring touchdowns. Every year, there's a debate about whether one tight end should be selected in the first round of fantasy football drafts. In 2026, that player is McBride. For what it's worth, managers are typically drafting him closer to the mid-second round, as he currently owns an ADP of 18.95. Nevertheless, he's a very appealing draft target considering how much production he offers at the tight end position relative to other tight ends in the league.

2.name: Brock Bowers
2.comment: A knee injury slowed Bowers last year, missing five games. He had some big numbers when on the field, catching 64 passes for 680 yards and seven touchdowns. Bowers was 11th overall in fantasy tight end scoring despite missing time. He had two 100-yard games and seven recaching double-digit fantasy points. Bowers is the top target in this passing game and gets a legit quarterback throwing him passes this year. This should be a huge plus for his production going forward. Bowers is a dynamic player at the tight end spot and already one of the best in all of football. He has very good speed for the position and runs tough routes. He also is very strong and does well with the contested catch, making him a tough cover. Bowers isn't a top notch blocker but continues to improve in that area.
2.outlook: Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers entered the 2025 campaign as the TE1 following his historic debut season the year prior, in which he caught 112 of his 153 targets for 1,194 yards and five touchdowns. However, the former Georgia standout suffered a knee injury in their Week 1 loss to the Patriots, which sidelined him for the rest of the season. While the 23-year-old tight end would only sit out five games (with two of them being Weeks 17 and 18), Bowers was not as dominant as he was the year before. In 2025, playing in one of the game's worst offensive units, Bowers brought in just 64 of his 86 targets for 680 yards and seven touchdowns. Much of his production came in Week 9 when he caught 12 passes for 127 yards and three scores. Entering 2026, Bowers' outlook looks far more favorable as he has already begun participating in team OTAs, suggesting this injury is far behind him. The 6-foot-4 pass catcher is slotted to be Las Vegas' primary pass catcher, as their WR room, led by Jalen Nailor and Tre Tucker, has minimal experience as a top target. While the QB play under rookie Fernando Mendoza or veteran Kirk Cousins could be unstable at times, Bowers projects to see a massive target share, which may not only lead the tight end position, but potentially all pass catchers as well. He carries elite value at his current ADP on Sleeper (25), sitting just outside the first two rounds.

3.name: Harold Fannin Jr.
3.comment: The Browns were a mess throwing the ball last year but that didn't slow Fannin. He had a big rookie season, emerging as the go-to tight end and target for the passing game. Fannin was sixth overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He had 72 receptions for 731 yards and seven total touchdowns. Fannin reached double-digit fantasy points five straight games to end his season. He will start from day one this year for the Browns. Fannin is really good after the catch and runs top routes for such a young player. Fannin also is not a bad blocker and has room for improvement in that area. He also has good hands and toughness on the contested catch.
3.outlook: After a hyper-productive final collegiate season at Bowling Green, Cleveland Browns tight end Harold Fannin Jr. wasted no time putting up counting stats in his rookie season as a pro, either. Fannin Jr. led the Browns' passing attack in receptions (72), targets (107), receiving yards (731), and tied Quinshon Judkins (ankle) for the team lead in scrimmage touchdowns (seven). The 6'4" tight end became a security blanket for the team's revolving door of quarterbacks around the line of scrimmage with a low average depth of target (6.0 aDOT). With a new head coach in Todd Monken and a scoring unit that added left tackle Spencer Fano, plus wide receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, in April's NFL Draft. There is optimism that the Browns' offense could be dramatically improved in 2026. That would help offset the obvious drawback of added competition for targets from Concepcion and Boston. Notably, the team let tight end David Njoku walk in free agency, and Njoku led the team in red-zone target share (20.5%). Fannin could see more work in the red zone for an offense that scores at a greater clip due to its improvements. Fannin is currently Rotoballer's 81st-ranked overall player in addition to his TE5 slot in terms of positional standing, which means his mid-sixth-round Sleeper ADP might be a tough sell. Reasons for optimism about the second-year player's talent and scoring role are definitely valid. Still, in redraft formats, he's ultimately at the mercy of how productive either Deshaun Watson or Shedeur Sanders can become in Monken's run-first system.

4.name: Colston Loveland
4.comment: Loveland was 12th overall in fantasy tight end scoring as a rookie. He started his year slow but really got it going late. He had double-digit targets his last four games of the season (two in the regular season and two in the playoffs). Loveland really got his footing the second half of the season, reaching 20-plus points three of his last 10 regular season games. He had over 700 yards and six touchdown on the year. It was an impressive rookie season. Loveland looks to be a huge part of this offense for years to come. Loveland is a great athlete for the position that plays like a big receiver more than a tight end. He is a tough cover because of his size and speed. Loveland is a load to bring down after the catch. He is a real smooth route runner for such a young player. Loveland also is a solid blocker, which will keep him on the field.
4.outlook: It took some time - nine weeks to be exact - for Colston Loveland to make an impact, but his 6-118-2 stat line against the Bengals was only the start of things to come. In a season in which the 2025 10th-overall pick had to overtake incumbent starter Cole Kmet and compete with a trio of talented wide receivers for targets, Loveland still finished his debut campaign with 58-713-6. It was in the most high-profile games, late in the season and in the postseason, when Loveland emerged as one of the league's best young tight ends. Loveland outtargeted Kmet 48 to 11 in the final four games of Chicago's season and topped 90 yards in three of those. When Loveland, Rome Odunze, and Luther Burden III, the new top weapons in Chicago following DJ Moore's trade to Buffalo, were on the field together, the tight end commanded a 33% target rate. Loveland is now ranked as a top-five tight end, with the fantasy football community wondering how high he can fly.

5.name: Isaiah Likely
5.comment: Likely saw his numbers take a bit of a dip last year in a Ravens passing game that had some struggles. He had 27 receptions, which was the lowest total of his career. He had just two games reaching double-digit fantasy points. There were several games he went without even getting a reception. Likely was more hit or miss than expected. He signed a big deal with the Giants this season to get a chance to start for the first time in his career. He reunites with his old coach, John Harbaugh. Likely is going to play a big role in an emerging Giants passing game. Likely is a big-play threat at tight end that can stretch the field in a hurry. He plays a little more like a receiver than a tight end. He needs work as a blocker, though, and will drop some passes.
5.outlook: New York Giants tight end Isaiah Likely steps into a featured role after John Harbaugh saw what he was capable of in Baltimore, but can we get consistent production here? He was limited by injuries in 2025, both to himself and Lamar Jackson, which led to just 27 catches for 307 yards and one touchdown. Likely required surgery to repair a broken bone in his foot, which shelved him through August and forced him to miss the first three games of the season. But alongside the overall offensive depression, he was far behind Derrick Henry, Mark Andrews, and Zay Flowers. Though the Giants' offense will be different than '25, if Likely goes from last year's 53% route participation rate toward Theo Johnson's 73% mark, we could be very happy. Mix in that Malik Nabers (knee) is no sure bet to recover, and the 6-foot-4 Likely could find himself with a prominent role with lots of red-zone attention. Though it's been nearly two years since he dominated the Chiefs for 111 yards and a TD (nearly two, those pesky toes) in Week 1 of 2024, the 26-year-old has a ceiling that most TEs don't possess. As a result of the talent, the Harbaugh connection, and the path to more involvement, his RotoBaller rank as the half-PPR TE12 is close to his TE11 ADP (pick 107) in late June.

6.name: Kyle Pitts
6.comment: Pitts had arguable his best season as a pro, finally getting back to his big ways. He was second overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He had a career-high 88 receptions on the season. Pitts also had a career-best five touchdowns. Pitts reached double-digit fantasy points nine of 17 games. He also dropped just two passes all season despite getting targeted 118 times. It was quite the season for Pitts. He should remain a huge part of this Falcons passing game going forward. He has been in the league five years but is just 25 years old. Pitts had 50-plus receptions three of five seasons. Pitts has big-time talent at the position. He has good hands and is very athletic. Pitts will make the tough catch in traffic. His combination of speed and size makes him a very tough cover at tight end. He still needs some work on his blocking but has made strides in that area.
6.outlook: Ever since being selected fourth overall in the 2021 NFL Draft, Kyle Pitts Sr. has had high expectations. He surpassed 1,000 receiving yards as a rookie, but has not hit the mark since and has routinely been considered a fantasy bust. However, Pitts exploded over the final six weeks of the 2025 season, averaging 8.5 targets, 6.5 receptions, 78.2 yards, and scored four touchdowns, finally rewarding fantasy managers en route to finishing as the TE2 on the season. Pitts should be in line for another heavy dose of targets, as the Falcons did not do much outside of adding rookie Zachariah Branch to the receiving room. Whether Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr. wins the quarterback job in Atlanta, fantasy managers should expect a healthy target share for the star tight end.

7.name: Tyler Warren
7.comment: Warren was already one of the top fantasy tight ends in the game in his rookie season. He was fifth overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He was a consistent factor in this offense from day one. He had 76 receptions for 817 yards and five total touchdowns. Warren reached double-digit fantasy points eight of 17 games. Warren is going to be a huge part of this offense for years to come. Warren is a big asset in the passing game and also helps as a blocker. Warren is a great athlete for a man of his size. He plays with toughness and does really well after the catch and on contested catches. He does a really good job of getting in and out of his breaks. Warren isn't a great downfield threat.
7.outlook: Warren is a solid TE1. The only concern is his quarterback play this year with Daniel Jones returning from a major injury. If the quarterback position has any issues, Warren could be impacted. Because of that, we would downgrade his numbers a tad from last year. Look for around 70 receptions for 800 yards and six touchdowns.

8.name: Travis Kelce
8.comment: Kelce continues to get it done and show few signs of slowing down a lot. He was third overall in fantasy tight end scoring. Kelce had 76 receptions for 851 yards and five touchdowns. The Chiefs did well in limiting his workload a little more to ensure he stays fresh throughout the season. Kelce had double-digit fantasy points nine of 17 games. He was a little more inconsistent than past years, though, having two games with just a catch. Kelce has topped 820 yards all but his rookie season in the NFL. He is 36 years old but remains one of the top tight ends in the game. Kelce remains the favorite target of Patrick Mahomes. Kelce is a big target with speed, athleticism and plus hands. He also is a good blocker. He really is a complete package at tight end. Kelce remains one of the best all-around tight ends in the game.
8.outlook: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce looks to prove the naysayers wrong going into his 14th NFL season at 37 years old. Though he played all 17 games, his usage was scaled back, resulting in his fewest targets (108) and catches (76) since 2015. The average depth of target remained steady at 6.8, but his route participation rate fell roughly three percentage points. His 851 yards still edged last year's 823 on 21 fewer catches, with five TDs surpassing the career-low of three in '24. Kelce did so on just 12 red-zone targets, compared to 25 the year before. While the Chiefs took a teamwide step back last year, his dip in scoring output is a longer trend. The last three years (48 games) have conferred 13 total TDs, which is a stark decline after scoring 12 times in '22 alone. His late-June half-PPR ADP near pick 104 (TE10) reflects confidence in both Kelce and Kansas City, while RotoBaller's 121st overall rank would have drafters think twice about the selection.

9.name: Tucker Kraft
9.comment: A torn ACL marred an otherwise really good season from Kraft. He was great in the eight games he played, catching 32 passes for 489 yards and six touchdowns. Kraft was 24th overall in fantasy tight end scoring despite playing about half the season. Kraft reached double-digit fantasy points five of eight games. Kraft has a long road back but a good chance to be healthy for the start of the year, barring any setbacks. Kraft has at least 30 receptions all three seasons in the NFL. Kraft is a big tight end that can help as a blocker and receiver. He is a pretty complete tight end for a young player. Kraft is tough to bring down after the catch and does well on contested catches. He lacks a little speed and his route running is just alright, but he is more than capable of the big play. Kraft might be the top big-play tight end in the game, averaging more than 15 yards per reception last year.
9.outlook: A mid-season ACL tear prevented Tucker Kraft from truly breaking out in his third professional season, but he was well on his way. The former third-round pick caught 30 of his 41 targets for 469 yards and six touchdowns across seven games. His 15.3 yards per reception ranked first among qualified tight ends, while he ranked second in yards per target and yards per route run. His target share (18.8%), however, left a little to be desired, but offseason roster changes can bump that number up. Target leader Romeo Doubs and rotational piece Dontayvion Wicks have moved on, and Green Bay didn't add any replacements for their outgoing receivers. On paper, Kraft and Christian Watson are the team's best weapons in the passing game. As long as Kraft is medically cleared by Week 1, which is the goal, the 25-year-old should rank inside the top five tight ends in redraft leagues.

10.name: Juwan Johnson
10.comment: Johnson continues to ascend in the Saints offense, building on his breakout season from the previous year. He had a huge season, catching 77 passes for 889 yards and three touchdowns. Johnson was eighth overall in fantasy tight end scoring. If he ends the end zone just a few more times, Johnson might have been a top-five tight end. He had double-digit fantasy points 10 of 17 games. He has become a huge part of the Saints up and coming passing attack. Johnson plays more like a receiver than a tight end. He has good speed and size. He runs solid routes and can stretch the field because of his speed and length. He does lack some consistency and will drop some passes (six last season).
10.outlook: New Orleans Saints tight end Juwan Johnson enters his age-30 campaign having just blown past his career-best marks with 102 targets, 77 catches, and 889 yards. This only led to three touchdowns, but one can't help but feel bullish with such enticing volume. He came out of the gate hot, finishing Weeks 1 and 2 as the TE4 and TE3, respectively. In fact, he'd be the TE13 or greater in seven of his first 10 games, and 10 of the 17 tilts overall. The Saints waited until the middle of Week 8 to flip Tyler Shough in at quarterback, all while the running back group dealt with injuries and ineffectiveness, so the second half is a better indicator for 2026 expectations. And between Weeks 9-17, Johnson's 9.6 half-PPR fantasy points per game was the seventh-best tally (min. 5 games) even without a single end-zone target in that span. His two TDs in that window were caught 5-10 yards out, and he looked like a secondary read on both plays. In fact, Johnson only had one end-zone target all year, and no Saint had more than three outside of Chris Olave (14!). If they funnel action to Olave, or newcomers Jordyn Tyson and Oscar Delp, and don't let Johnson eat in the red zone, then fantasy managers will be disappointed given the half-PPR ADP at the 139th pick (TE17). Our rank around pick 150 bakes in a bit more volatility.

11.name: Jake Ferguson
11.comment: Ferguson set career highs in receptions (82) and touchdowns (eight). He was fourth overall in fantasy tight end scoring. It was his best fantasy season to date. Ferguson was super consistent, having double-digit fantasy points nine of 17 games. He didn't make a lot of big plays in the passing game but got a ton of looks and was a top red-zone target. Ferguson has at least 59 receptions three straight seasons. He is the starter for the Cowboys and a big part of the passing game. Ferguson is a solid pass catcher and blocker. He isn't exceptional in any area but more than holds his own. He has plus hands and is a willing blocker. Drops were a bit of an issue for him the last three years, having six each of those seasons.
11.outlook: Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson has finished as the TE8 in two of his last three seasons, most recently posting 600 yards on a career-high 82 receptions while scoring 8 times. At RotoBaller's TE13 heading into 2026 drafts, he's going later than what he has already shown to be somewhat of a baseline, and under the right circumstances, he's capable of putting up week-winning performances. With five-time Pro Bowl receiver CeeDee Lamb missing time early in the year with a high ankle sprain, Ferguson became a safety blanket for quarterback Dak Prescott, seeing the fourth most targets in the league through the first five weeks of the season, and pacing as the fantasy TE1 through Week 7. The presence of Lamb and 2025 breakout George Pickens is enough to keep Feguson from cracking the top-12, but should either miss time in 2026, the former fourth-rounder out of Wisconsin has insurance upside rare to the position, capable of stepping into a top-two role in one of the league's most potent offenses without looking out of place. Even with Dallas' two Pro Bowl receivers at full health, Ferguson's floor is still high enough to more than justify his 10th-round ADP. In the 11 games in which all three players saw a normal workload in 2025, Ferguson made at least five catches in seven. With the Cowboys' focus through free agency and the NFL Draft squarely on the defensive side of the ball, Ferguson's role should look familiar entering his fifth season in Dallas. For 2026 drafters opting to wait on tight end, the 27-year-old profiles as a can't-miss late-round pick, both for his reliable volume-based floor and legitimate top-five upside.

12.name: Sam LaPorta
12.comment: LaPorta missed about half the season because of a herniated disc. He was having a pretty good season before getting hurt, catching 40 passes for 489 yards and three touchdowns. He reached double-digit fantasy points five of nine games. LaPorta had two straight seasons with 60 or more receptions before last year. He is a big part of the Lions passing game. LaPorta catches the ball well and is a volume tight end, racking up the catches on a weekly basis. He is a good route runner and willing blocker. He also will make plays after the catch and is a much improved pass catcher, dropping just a pass the last two years.
12.outlook: Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta was the half-PPR TE7 through Week 9, securing 40 catches for 489 yards and three TDs, before ongoing back pains culminated in a fully herniated disc, ending his year in Week 10. He had initially tried to rehab it, but surgery was ultimately necessary after a month off didn't solve things. And Dan Campbell said that LaPorta is "trending the right way" amidst a mid-June minicamp practice. Given that LaPorta is holding onto a half-PPR ADP around pick 80 in June as the No. 8 TE, it seems the market is echoing Campbell's positive statements. A healthy Lions team has many mouths to feed, so looking at that electric rookie campaign with 120 targets and 10 TDs sets unrealistic expectations. But his prominent role in a high-scoring offense does afford a lofty ceiling and median outcome that is well worth his current price tag in most draft rooms.

13.name: Mark Andrews
13.comment: Andrews had a disappointing season in a Ravens passing game that had more struggles than normal. He played a full season but had just 48 receptions for 422 yards and five touchdowns. Andrews was just 17th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. His numbers have decreased some in recent seasons, failing to top 55 receptions three straight years. The good news for Andrews is Isaiah Likely is gone, which could lead to more looks and playing time for Andrews. Andrews remains a top target in the Ravens passing game and favorite target of Lamar Jackson. Andrews is a big target that does well after the catch for a man of his size. He can be a big-play threat in the passing game. He will drop a few passes and isn't a top blocking tight end but that doesn't hold him back much at all.
13.outlook: Baltimore Ravens tight end Mark Andrews struggled to produce much in 2025. He was in a hideous rotation with two other tight ends, Isaiah Likely and Charlie Kolar, that both departed the team in free agency. The Ravens drafted two tight ends, Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas, in the 2026 NFL Draft, but mid-to-late round draft picks tend to be brought along slowly into offenses. Perhaps the Ravens will pass more heavily to their receivers, now that they drafted WRs Elijah Sarratt and JaKobi Lane, but this year's crop of pass-catchers was rather weak historically. Andrews could see his number called more as a matter of necessity. Andrews' separation metrics were elite as recently as 2024. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson tends to spread the ball around heavily, so there's risk in drafting Andrews in fantasy, but there's enough theoretical upside for a late-round dart throw. He's still an effective red zone weapon.

14.name: Dalton Kincaid
14.comment: Kincaid once again showed flashes of a breakout season but injuries were an issue, missing five games. He had some big games when on the field, though, finishing with 39 receptions for 571 yards and five touchdowns. If he plays a full year, Kincaid has 55 receptions for 809 yards and seven touchdowns. Kincaid had five games with double-digit fantasy points. And he scored touchdowns each of the Bills two playoff games. Kincaid produced good numbers, reaching the 100-yard mark two times. He will be the top pass-catching tight end for the Bills, getting plenty of work. He has 39 or more receptions all three of his seasons in the NFL. Kincaid is a top athlete that runs routes like a receiver and his speed causes plenty of mismatches in coverage. He can make the big play or just move the chains as a reliable target for Josh Allen. Kincaid is not much of a blocker for the position.
14.outlook: Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid missed five games last season with lingering hamstring, oblique, and knee issues. His health has bothered him for the past two seasons, causing limited usage even when healthy. However, he has stated that he feels good heading into 2026. Kincaid's best statistical season thus far in his career came as a rookie in 2023, when he caught 73 passes for 673 yards and two scores. He did record five touchdown receptions last season, but was limited to 39 grabs for 571 yards. The addition of DJ Moore should free up more space for Kincaid to operate with when healthy, but his snaps may be limited with Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes still on the roster as stronger blocking tight ends. He is currently being drafted as a low-end TE1, which is closer to his floor than his ceiling should he stay healthy.

15.name: David Njoku
15.comment: Njoku had some injury issues but also took a backseat to rookie Harold Fannin much of the season. He had one of his worst seasons as a pro, catching 33 passes for 293 yards and four touchdowns. He had 55-plus receptions three straight seasons before last year. He will look to regain a starting role this season and get back to his numbers of past years after signing with the Chargers. Njoku has great size, speed and strength for the position. He can get downfield in a hurry and turn a short pass into a big play. Njoku also is a willing blocker. He will struggle with drops at times and isn't the best route runner at this stage of his career.
15.outlook: Njoku might be a good buy-low candidate. He has been a top-15 fantasy tight end three of the last four seasons. His track record suggests he can get it going again. Take him as a top backup and hope for a rebound. He could get 60 receptions for 600 yards and five touchdowns.

16.name: George Kittle
16.comment: Kittle started the season banged up and ended it with a major injury, tearing his Achilles' during the playoffs. But while he was on the field, Kittle posted big numbers. He played 11 games but still managed to finish 13th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He had four games with 20-plus fantasy points. He might lead all of fantasy tight ends in scoring if he is able to play a full year. He had two straight 1,000-yard seasons before last year. Kittle has a long road back from a major injury but should be back shortly after the start of the season. He is expected to miss some time, though. Kittle is one of the top tight ends in the game. Kittle isn't a flashy player but a playmaker. He runs solid routes and has great hands. Kittle is a much improved blocker from earlier in his career. He lacks a little explosion for the position and uses his strength more than anything when it comes to catching the ball and blocking. He also has surprising speed.
16.outlook: San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle (Achilles) caught 57 of 69 targets for 628 yards and seven touchdowns in 2025. Having missed six games due to injury, his overall production lagged behind his peers, but he was the second-ranked tight end in fantasy points per game. Unfortunately, his season came to a devastating end when he ruptured his right Achilles tendon in the Wild Card round of the playoffs. Despite the serious injury, Kittle's stated goal is to play in Week 1 of the 2026 season. The condition and location of the rupture - a clean tear in an area with high blood flow - allow for quicker healing and optimism that the two-time All-Pro can beat the typical recovery timeline of nine to twelve months. The question of exactly when Kittle will be game-ready, not to mention what condition he will be in, has contributed to a hefty discount in early fantasy football drafts compared to past years. A return to form is no guarantee, but given Kittle's prominence in the 49ers' passing attack, rolling the dice on him shouldn't be out of the question. Kittle is the TE15 in RotoBaller's current rankings.

17.name: T.J. Hockenson
17.comment: Like most of the options in the passing game for the Vikings, Hockenson disappointed last year. He had 51 receptions for just 438 yards and three touchdowns. It might have been the worst season of his career, averaging just 8.6 yards per reception. He had 85-plus receptions each of the last two seasons he has played a full year. Hockenson remains the top tight end for the Vikings and could be involved in a much better passing game with Kyler Murray likely leading the way. Hockenson is a pretty complete tight end. Hockenson is a very athletic tight end that does it all at the position. He catches the ball well, can make plays down the field and is a solid blocker.
17.outlook: Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson struggled to 51 catches on 66 targets for 438 yards and three touchdowns in 2025, as part of a teamwide dip in production. He also missed the final two games due to a shoulder injury. The inconsistent quarterbacking left much to be desired, but Hock still appears to have lost a step since his major knee injury in 2023. The veteran wound up with 17 fewer yards on 10 more catches thanks to a depressed 5.2 average depth of target (8.4 in '24, 7.7 in '23), per Pro Football Reference, and limited ability to shed tacklers and create yards after the catch. Of 19 TEs with 50 or more catches last season, Hock's 1.53 yards after contact per reception ranked 14th, and his 9% drop rate was the second-worst mark according to Fantasy Points Data. Those who believe that Kyler Murray will deliver with far greater accuracy and efficiency could see many of those numbers improve, even if Hockenson's own burst doesn't ever mirror his pre-injury prime. RotoBaller's TE22 half-PPR rank is identical to his ADP price, except we have him going 20 picks later on the other side of a tier jump. Believers can snag him late, though most will not feel comfortable with him as their starter.

18.name: Hunter Henry
18.comment: Henry had maybe his best season as a pro in the Patriots much-improved offense. He was a top-10 fantasy tight end, finishing ninth overall. He had 60 receptions for 768 yards and seven touchdowns. Henry has 60-plus receptions each of the last two seasons. Henry had eight of 17 games with double-digit fantasy points. Henry should continue to play a big role as the starting tight end for the Patriots. He has formed a good rapport with Drake Maye. Henry is a pretty complete tight end. He is a good athlete and does well as a blocker. He runs good routes and is athletic enough to make plenty of big plays.
18.outlook: New England Patriots tight end Hunter Henry led the team with seven receiving touchdowns last season. Henry logged a career-high 708 receiving yards on 60 catches over 17 games. The 31-year-old has shown no signs of slowing down and owned 33.3% of the team's targets in the red zone. Henry is durable as they come and has logged 81 of 85 games for the Patriots. New England released Stefon Diggs, but added wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason. On top of Brown and Doubs, Henry will also compete for targets with Kayshon Boutte, DeMario Douglas, and Kyle Williams. The Patriots did let tight end Austin Hooper walk in free agency, but drafted Eli Raridon in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Henry has been quarterback Drake Maye's most reliable target in the red zone, and even with the recent additions, his role around the goal line shouldn't change much. Henry finished as TE7 in fantasy football last year, but is ranked as RotoBaller's TE18, making him more of a streaming option in a positive matchup than a weekly starter in 2026.

19.name: Kenyon Sadiq
19.comment: The Jets picked Sadiq at the end of the first round. The talented tight end should make an immediate impact his rookie year. The Jets are going to find ways to get him the ball whether as a tight end or lining him up as a receiver. He will be a tough cover. Sadiq has great size, speed and strength for the position. He can play more like a receiver than a tight end. Sadiq also makes a lot of plays after the catch for the tight end. He is not much of a blocker for a tight end but gives good effort and can improve in that area.
19.outlook: With the addition of tight end Kenyon Sadiq, the New York Jets could be looking to move to more 12-personnel sets this season to create mismatches with both Sadiq and former second-round selection Mason Taylor under the guidance of new offensive coordinator Frank Reich. Of the two tight ends, Sadiq offers the higher upside coming off a Junior season at Oregon that saw him haul in 51 passes for 560 receiving yards, averaging 11.0 Yards per reception, and find the end zone on eight occasions. Last season, the Jets ranked 29th in total yards per game (263.6) and were last in passing yards per game, averaging a minuscule 140.3. With Breece Hall extended and Garrett Wilson healthy (knee), the additions of Sadiq, Geno Smith, and Omar Cooper Jr. have many projecting a significant improvement for the Jets this season. Look for Sadiq to operate from the slot and become one of Smith's first reads in the passing game, as his 1.72 yards per route run throughout his college tenure compares favorably to those of Trey McBride (1.65) and Sam LaPorta (1.75). First-round draft capital and an early declaration have historically led to production at the tight end position, both of which Sadiq has entering the 2026 season. Sadiq has an ADP of 117 on Sleeper, making him slightly overvalued relative to his current RotoBaller overall ranking of 130.

20.name: Chigoziem Okonkwo
20.comment: There was hope that Okonkwo might take his game to a new level last year with Cam Ward taking over as the starting quarterback, but it was more of the same for him. He did set a career high in receptions (56) but those totals weren't that much different than his previous two seasons. Okonkwo was 21st overall in fantasy tight end scoring for the second straight season. He has three straight seasons reaching 50-plus receptions. He signed with the Commanders this offseason to become their top tight end. He has a chance to play a big role with his new team. Okonkwo is a great athlete with top speed. His route running needs some work and he isn't much of a blocker, but his athletic ability at the position makes him a tough cover. He will drop some passes, having 17 drops in four seasons.
20.outlook: Washington Commanders tight end Chig Okonkwo arrives in the nation's capital with a three-year, $27 million contract and the promise of the most competent quarterback play of his young career. Since coming into the league in 2022 as a fourth-round pick of the Tennessee Titans, Okonkwo has never been part of an offense with a quarterback throwing for more than 3,200 yards or 15 touchdowns. Even while setting career highs and leading the Titans in receptions and yards in 2025, that only amounted to 560 yards on 56 catches, as Tennessee's 191 passing yards per game ranked 29th in the league. While injuries derailed his sophomore campaign, Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels threw for 3,568 yards and 25 touchdowns as 2024's Offensive Rookie of the Year, supporting a then 33-year-old Zach Ertz to a TE8 half-PPR finish. Washington spent a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft on Clemson slot receiver Antonio Williams and added third-down running back Rachaad White to an imbalanced group of pass catchers behind two-time Pro Bowler Terry McLaurin. Even with McLaurin missing seven games in 2025, his 38 receptions still top the list of returning players, with running back Jeremy McNichols and 2025 fourth-round pick Jaylin Lane slotting in at a respective second and third with 41 combined catches. Ertz is no longer with the team, presenting Okonkwo with the opportunity to step right in as the second option in a David Blough passing attack sure to borrow elements from the heavy under-center, play-action offenses of Ben Johnson and Kevin O'Connell. At RotoBaller's TE22, Okonkwo is regularly falling to the final rounds of 2026 drafts, if selected at all, but he represents a high-upside bargain for managers opting not to spend up at the position, and could realistically crack the top 10 if Daniels plays anything close to a full 17-game slate.

21.name: Brenton Strange
21.comment: If not for injury issues, missing five games, Strange might have been a top-10 fantasy tight end last season. He finished 23rd overall in fantasy tight end scoring, playing 12 games. He had six of 12 games with double-digit fantasy points. Strange had 46 receptions for 540 yards and three touchdowns. He has two straight seasons reaching 40 or more receptions. Strange has emerged as the top tight end in the Jaguars much-improved passing game. Strange is a good blocking tight end but also has speed and is a good athlete. He is a physical player that is tough to bring down after the catch. He will drop some passes and could sharpen his route running a little but continues to make strides in both areas.
21.outlook: Jacksonville Jaguars tight end Brenton Strange turned a 12-game season into 46 catches on 60 targets for 540 yards and three touchdowns. He routinely ran snap counts of 75% or higher, but his early, pre-injury volume yielded zero touchdowns in those first five games. In fact, he didn't even see a single red-zone target! However, he had 11 RZ looks from Week 12 on, which led the team and made him the half-PPR TE8. That late trend and the overall upward trajectory for Jacksonville's offense make him a reasonable breakout target for those who want to wait at the position. But the strong WR corps cannot be ignored, and it contributed to his lower 64.2% route participation rate (compared to most of the TEs drafted earlier). Even though the 1.89 yards per route run is strong, volume often rules the day. His half-PPR ADP of 140 (TE18) and RotoBaller rank of 149 balance that ceiling proposition with the fact that you're speculating on an unproven half-season on an offense with four playmakers at wide receiver.

22.name: Pat Freiermuth
22.comment: Freiermuth had a disappointing season, splitting a lot of the work at tight end with Jonnu Smith. He had just 41 receptions for 486 yards and four touchdowns, finishing 25th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He reached double-digit fantasy points just three games. Freiermuth has 60-plus receptions three of five seasons. He could get a lot more targets this year with Smith gone. Freiermuth has really good size and hands for the position. He is not a huge big-play threat but does well in getting open and moving the chains. He still needs some work on his blocking and will struggle at times with consistency.
22.outlook: Pittsburgh Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth had his share of standout moments in 2025, but he still turned in the least productive season of his five-year career on a per-game basis. After setting a career-high with 65 receptions in 2024, Freiermuth managed just 41 catches on 54 targets with Aaron Rodgers at quarterback last season. Although Rodgers is set to return for one final year in Pittsburgh, much of Freiermuth's situation will look different in 2026. Jonnu Smith, who was significantly less effective on 54 targets of his own last year, was released by the Steelers in March, while Connor Heyward departed in free agency. The Steelers signed Darnell Washington to a contract extension this offseason, but the 6-foot-7 former Georgia standout has proven himself as a blocking tight end rather than a pure receiving threat. Even with the additions of Michael Pittman Jr. and rookie Germie Bernard to the wide receiver room, Freiermuth could see an increase in playing time, and should also benefit from playing in new head coach Mike McCarthy's pass-friendly offense. The 27-year-old is unlikely to be drafted in most fantasy leagues this fall, but his early-season usage will be worth monitoring for managers in need of tight end help.

23.name: Cade Otton
23.comment: Otton had 59 receptions for a second straight season. He was 22nd overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He had five games with double-digit fantasy points. Otton got his weekly looks in the Bucs passing game and should continue to get his chances in this Bucs offense. And with the team losing a few players this offseason, Otton could see his targets increase a little. Otton has 40-plus receptions every season in the NFL. He is a good pass catcher with solid route running. He is a willing blocker, but still needs work in that area. Otton doesn't really wow in any area but is a reliable target that will move the chains.
23.outlook: Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Cade Otton is returning for his fifth year with the team in 2026. His 2025 campaign was buoyed by WR teammates Mike Evans, Chris Godwin, and Jalen McMillan all missing significant time. Nevertheless, Otton's stat line of 59 receptions on 81 targets for 572 yards and one touchdown represented a slight tick downward from his 2024 output. He ultimately finished as the TE22, his worst ranking since his rookie year. Evans is now in San Francisco, removing one obstacle for Otton, but Godwin and McMillan will enter the season healthy. The team's top wideout, sophomore Emeka Egbuka, is poised to step up further, too, and third-round rookie Ted Hurst also joins the receiving room. On the bright side for Otton, he had the highest snap share of any tight end in 2025, and the Buccaneers added no real competition for him at the position this offseason. Still, although Otton will see plenty of playing time, his target volume appears set to decrease. He is being drafted as the TE27, meaning he is nothing more than a late-round pick at this time. Prioritize other options to fill out your roster in your fantasy draft.

24.name: Dalton Schultz
24.comment: Schultz had maybe the best season of his career, finishing 10th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He had a career-high 82 receptions. He had nine of 17 games with double-digit fantasy points. He was a consistent target in the Texans passing attack. He has 53-plus receptions six straight seasons. Schultz will remain the top pass-catching tight end for the Texans. Cade Stover could cut into his playing time a little, though. Stover missed a good chunk of last season because of injury, leading to more work for Schultz. Schultz is a good move the chains tight end and reliable target in the passing game. He catches the ball well and runs decent routes. He lacks a little big-play ability, though, and some speed for the position. He also does do well as a blocker.
24.outlook: Houston Texans tight end Dalton Schultz set a new career-high with 82 catches last year, totaling 777 yards and three touchdowns in a middling passing environment. C.J. Stroud did not recover the form shown as a rookie in 2023, which left Schultz with 9.5 yards per catch (his lowest mark for a full season). This went down despite a career-long 47-yard reception that eclipsed his previous high of 32. Schultz also benefited from the lack of a true WR2, as they employed a revolving door of sorts behind Nico Collins, and there was no competition from a second TE (Cade Stover saw 16 targets). Jayden Higgins and Jaylin Noel entering Year 2, Tank Dell returning to play, David Montgomery improving the rushing outlook, drafting Marlin Klein in the second round, and signing Foster Moreau could all eat into the opportunity that Schultz enjoyed in '25. He should still bring a healthy floor to the table, but we may get the guy who had 50-60 catches in 2023-24 instead. As a result, his RotoBaller rank is near 175 as the TE24, slightly trailing the 163 ADP in half-PPR leagues.

25.name: Dallas Goedert
25.comment: Goedert finished top-10 in fantasy tight end scoring, mainly because of a career-high 11 touchdowns. He had Neve read more than five in a season before last year. He had a career-high 60 receptions as well. Goedert showed a little more consistency last year, having nine of 15 games with double-digit fantasy points. He re-signed with the Eagles after the season but now has rookie Eli Stowers to compete with for playing time. Goedert is likely to start again but is going to lose out on targets to the talented rookie. Goedert has 55-plus receptions four of five seasons. Goedert has been a big part of the Eagles offense throughout his career but struggled with injury often. He has played a full season just once in eight years. Goedert is a big tight end that blocks well along the line but also can make plays in the passing game. He is a big target that does well with contested catches. He can be a big-play threat at the tight end spot because of his size and speed.
25.outlook: Philadelphia Eagles tight end Dallas Goedert had an outstanding 2025 campaign, thanks to more than doubling his previous career-high mark with 11 touchdowns. He also set a personal best with 60 catches, albeit for only 591 yards, a far cry from 830 in '21 and only fourth-most during his eight-year tenure. While it is tough to buy into TD outliers, A.J. Brown's trade does remove the other most established red-zone weapon that Philly has utilized in recent years. The newer players will have to prove themselves and establish rapport with Jalen Hurts, while Goedert will be "Ol' Reliable." His team-leading 15 red-zone targets also illustrate that the TDs weren't necessarily fluky, or a result of others seeing more RZ volume but failing to convert. We still must expect regression on that front, but the 6-foot-5 TE should still see heavy utilization when it counts, especially if the red-zone rushing success does not rebound after a down '25. This new ceiling makes him an intriguing pick around his 120 half-PPR ADP as the TE14.

26.name: Gunnar Helm
26.comment: Helm played a backup role his rookie season and got a good amount of chances in that role. He had 44 receptions for 357 yards and two touchdowns, showing some good promise in year one. Helm had three games reaching double-digit fantasy points. Helm has a chance to be the starter for the Titans this year with Chig Okonkwo gone. Helm is a good route runner for a young player and can do really well down the seam. Helm will make some plays after the catch and does a good job of catching nearly everything his way. Helm is a decent blocker but it isn't an area that he excels.
26.outlook: Following an ankle sprain during his 40-yard dash at the 2025 combine, Tennessee Titans tight end Gunnar Helm has had an uphill climb to make an impact as a pro, but it seems to be slowly taking shape. As a fourth-round pick in last year's draft, Helm platooned at Tennessee's tight end spot with Chig Okonkwo to amass decent numbers as a rookie. He totaled 44 receptions on 55 targets for 357 yards and two touchdowns despite playing for the NFL's third-worst offense in passing yards per attempt (5.7 YPA). The team evidently saw enough in Helm through that action; Okonkwo signed with the Washington Commanders in March, and the team didn't draft a tight end in April until the seventh round. The former Texas standout's competition for receiving work at the position includes Daniel Bellinger and Kylen Granson - both of whom have fewer than 100 career receptions in at least three NFL seasons. The arrow seems to be pointing up for a Titans offense that added first-round rookie Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson at wide receiver, and Brian Daboll joins the team as offensive coordinator to call plays and develop Cam Ward. Helm will certainly slot behind Tate, Robinson, and veteran Calvin Ridley in Tennessee's target tree. Still, he'llhave a path to routes and relevance for an offense that could be significantly more functional in 2026. He is RotoBaller's 24th-ranked tight end in overall PPR rankings, fitting into a tier with T.J. Hockenson and Dalton Schultz as other tight ends with a monopoly on their teams' positional snaps but a limited chance to be a featured part of the offense. In dynasty formats, Helm could be a late-round dart that joins lineups in positive matchups, but he will need a productive year to avoid convincing the Titans to draft a replacement next spring.

27.name: Oronde Gadsden II
27.comment: Gadsden was a bit of a surprise his rookie season, emerging as the top tight end for the Chargers. He ended up 15th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. Gadsden had 664 yards, averaging an impressive 13.6 yards per reception. If there was a negative for Gadsden, he dropped five passes. Either way, Gadsden seems setup to be a top tight end in this offense for years to come. Gadsden is a good route runner for a tight end and uses his frame well to shield off defenders. He is still learning the position, though, and blocking can be an issue right now. He is a big-play threat, playing more like a receiver than a tight end.
27.outlook: Gadsden is an intriguing breakout candidate in the Chargers new offense. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel has a history of producing some big fantasy tight end numbers. Gadsden should be considered a low-end No. 1 fantasy tight end. Look for around 65 receptions for 800 yards and five touchdowns.

28.name: Eli Stowers
28.comment: The Eagles selected Stowers in the second round of this year's draft. He is a big-time athlete that can jump out of the building. He is best on seam routes and making big plays down the field. Stowers is not a polished product blocking and will need to improve in that area to be a three-down player in the NFL. Stowers has Dallas Goedert to compete with for playing time his rookie season but should become the starter sooner than later in this offense. This might be the last year Goedert is with the Eagles.
28.outlook: The Philadelphia Eagles made tight end Eli Stowers a second-round pick in April's Draft. The fit here is fantastic, as Stowers has a chance to establish himself in an offense undergoing plenty of change. All reports suggest that Philadelphia will be shipping No. 1 wide receiver A.J. Brown out of town in June, leaving plenty of room for other players to step up. Stowers is going to step in as a hyper-athletic tight end that offensive coordinators can only dream of coaching. He ran a 4.51 40-yard dash at the combine to go along with a massive 45.5-inch vertical jump. He will not start right away, but there is no doubt the Eagles will scheme plenty of looks for him throughout the season. Stowers could find consistent fantasy success if he can supplant fellow tight end Dallas Goedert on the depth chart. Goedert is getting older, and let's face it, he is not always healthy. When Goedert is on the field, he typically puts up solid numbers because of the way the Eagles use their tight ends. All Stowers needs is a slice of that pie, and he should begin to thrive. If Stowers gets going this year, the Eagles will be hard-pressed to keep him off the field.

29.name: Mike Gesicki
29.comment: Gesicki had injury issues last year, missing four games. He had 28 receptions for 307 yards and two touchdowns. His stats were way down from his first season in Cincinnati, a season he had 65 receptions. Gesicki had just two games all last season with double-digit fantasy points. It was a disappointing season. He should remain the top pass-catching tight end for the Bengals. Gesicki has four seasons for his career with 50-plus receptions. Gesicki plays more like a receiver than a tight end. He is a good athlete that just makes plays. He has very good hands and runs plus routes. He has dropped just 14 passes in eight seasons. He still is not much of a blocker, though, which will keep him off the field at times.
29.outlook: Cincinnati Bengals tight end Mike Gesicki had a forgettable year in 2025, but he did just enough at the tail end of the season to prove he'll still have streaming potential in 2026. Gesicki's 42 targets and 28 receptions marked the lowest totals since his rookie campaign, but the raw stats alone don't tell the full story. With quarterback Joe Burrow sidelined by Week 3 with a Grade 3 turf toe injury, Cincinnati's normally high-powered offense sputtered through the opening portion of the schedule with an ineffective Jake Browning under center. The team was able to get back on track offensively with a mid-season trade for Joe Flacco, but Gesicki suffered a pectoral injury two snaps into Flacco's first start with the Bengals and was placed on injured reserve. Gesicki got back onto the field around the same time as Burrow, and in their six games played together to end the year, Gesicki caught 16 passes for 211 yards and two touchdowns, good enough to make him TE15 over that stretch. With the Bengals forgoing the tight end position in free agency and adding only Jack Endries in the seventh round of the NFL Draft, Gesicki's biggest competition could come from 2024 fourth-round pick Erick All Jr., who missed the entirety of the 2025 season with a torn ACL and has not had a fully healthy season since 2021 at Michigan. Gesicki will have his occasional spike weeks while running a distant third behind Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, but should either miss time in 2026, Gesicki has proven himself capable of stepping into a number-two role of fantasy relevance. At RotoBaller's TE31, he's unlikely to be selected in many redraft leagues, but his early-season schedule bears monitoring as he will again enter the streaming conversation whenever the matchup dictates.

30.name: Jake Tonges
30.comment: Tonges was a big surprise for the 49ers last year, getting some chances to start because of injury to George Kittle. Tonges made some plays after failing to catch a pass his first three seasons in the NFL. He had 34 receptions for 293 yards and five touchdowns. He reached double-digit fantasy points four of his first six games but didn't hit the mark again after Week 6. Tonges is likely the top backup for the 49ers again this year and could find his way in the starting lineup early in the year with Kittle recovering from a major injury. Tonges is a good pass catcher that does well in the red zone. He is a solid move the chains target. He also has good hands, failing to drop a pass all last year.
30.outlook: Tonges could have some fantasy value early in the year if he is getting some starts. He showed last year that he can be a help to fantasy teams. Look for around 40 receptions for 400 yards and a few scores.

31.name: AJ Barner
31.comment: Barner was the starter from day one in year two. He had a solid season in that role, finishing 14th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He had seven total touchdowns and caught 52 passes. Barner had double-digit fantasy points eight of 17 games. He was even used a decent amount in short-yardage rushing situations and did well in that role, rushing 10 times for 14 yards and a score. Barner was able to hold off rookie Elijah Arroyo all of last season, but Arroyo is likely to challenge Barner for the right to start this year. Barner really helps as a blocker, which will get him on the field plenty. He can be a big help in the run game. Barner is not a top pass catcher but can help move the chains and make the occasional big play. He has improved in that area since entering the league.
31.outlook: Barner might have reached his ceiling last year. He has some touchdown potential even if Arroyo earns the starting job but his overall fantasy value is not too high. He might be worth a spot start in a pinch. He can get around 40 receptions for 400 yards and a four scores.

32.name: Mason Taylor
32.comment: Taylor had a decent rookie season, starting much of the year. He had 44 receptions for 369 yards and a touchdown in 13 games. He reached double-digit fantasy points four games. Taylor showed flashes of good things but was part of a passing game that really struggled. A stable quarterback situation could be a plus for him in year two. But the addition of rookie Kenyon Sadiq really clouds things for Taylor going forward. Taylor might still start but is going to lose out on targets because of Sadiq. Taylor is a top athlete that can help on all three levels. He isn't the most physical tight end and doesn't do a whole lot after the catch. He is more of a volume target at this stage of his career.
32.outlook: Taylor is not too appealing anymore with Sadiq added to the mix. He probably isn't draft material anymore. Look for around 40 receptions for 400 yards and a few touchdowns.

33.name: Jonnu Smith
33.comment: A move to Pittsburgh was not a good one for Smith last year. He rotated with a group of tight ends and saw a big downturn in production from the previous season. He had 38 receptions for 222 yards and two scores, finishing 35th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. Smith will look to regain the magic from the previous season but might be destined to continue to serve more of a backup role. Smith is a solid all-around talent at tight end. He can make plays in the passing game but also does well as a blocker along the line. Smith does well after the catch, showing big-play ability in the passing game. He does lack some polish with his route running and will drop some passes.
33.outlook: Smith was a huge bust last season. He might do a little better this year but don't expect a huge turnaround. He might get 40 catches for 400 yards and a few scores, making him a deep reserve for fantasy teams.

34.name: Evan Engram
34.comment: There were some high hopes for Engram in his first season with Denver but he never got it going. He had 50 receptions for 461 yards and a touchdown. Engram was just 29th overall in fantasy tight end scoring, having two games with double-digit fantasy points. His big game were few and far between. The Broncos younger, more exciting options got a lot more work. Engram has two seasons with 70-plus receptions for his career but his best days might be behind him at age 31. He will continue to get some chances in this passing game but has plenty to compete with for targets. Engram plays more like a receiver than a tight end. He is a top athlete that does well in making the acrobatic catch. Engram lacked consistency early in his career but has done much better in that area in recent seasons.
34.outlook: Engram was a bust last year. A sudden turnaround in year two in an offense that has added even more weapons to the passing game would be a surprise for Engram. He might get 40 receptions for 400 yards and a few scores.

35.name: Zach Ertz
35.comment: Ertz was having another productive season as the starter for the Commanders before tearing his ACL in Week 14. He had 50 receptions for 504 yards and four touchdowns in 13 games. He was 19th overall in fantasy tight end scoring, having double-digit fantasy points five games. Ertz is 35 years old and recovering from a torn ACL, so he has some concerns for this coming year. A starting job is not guaranteed for him. Ertz has at least 70 receptions and 750 yards six of 11 seasons. Ertz isn't really a speed demon at tight end but runs very good routes and has solid hands. He also blocks pretty well but isn't an elite blocker by any means. He does lack a little speed to create big plays down the field but makes up for that with his hands and route running.
35.outlook: Ertz is a risk for the coming season. Age and injuries are a concern. He might be worth a shot as a No. 2 fantasy tight end as long as you have a solid starter already on your roster. Ertz could be a factor later in the season once he gets back up to speed. He can get around 40 catches for 400 yards and a couple scores.

36.name: Elijah Arroyo
36.comment: Arroyo played a backup role his rookie season, playing behind A.J. Barner much of the year. Arroyo did get a few chances, though, catching 15 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown. He could move up the depth chart this year and challenge Barner for the starting job. A new offensive coaching staff could be a positive for Arroyo. Arroyo runs routes more like a receiver than a tight end. He is a good athlete with plus size and speed. Arroyo is a willing blocker but needs some work in that area to be a more complete tight end.
36.outlook: Arroyo is a bit of a wild card but certainly has a high ceiling if he earns the starting job in this Seahawks offense. He is worth a late-round look come draft day. He might get 30 receptions for 400 yards and a few touchdowns.

37.name: Max Klare
37.comment: The Rams took Klare in the second round of this year's draft. He has a lot to compete with at tight end but could emerge as a top pass-catching threat in this high-powered Rams offense. Klare is a very good route runner for a young player. He knows how to get open and find the soft spot in coverages. He also has enough speed to stretch the field. Klare also isn't a bad blocker and won't be a liability in that area. He will drop some passes, though.
37.outlook: Expectations at the tight end position have never been higher in fantasy after Colston Loveland, Tyler Warren, and Harold Fannin Jr. ultimately became their team's top receiving threat last season, as rookies. Historically, the tight end position has been one of the last in terms of fantasy development, and fantasy managers should remain patient when evaluating what they have in Max Klare. Klare comes into a Rams' tight end room that is already crowded with the likes of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, and Terrance Ferguson already in tow. While the outlook is not great for Klare in 2026, he possesses one of the top athletic profiles among the tight ends drafted in April's draft, and as a Junior at Purdue, he caught 51 passes for 684 receiving yards, averaging 2.22 yards per route run. Klare transferred to Ohio State in 2025, where he once again proved his worth as a pass catcher, averaging 10.4 yards per reception, hauling in 43 passes for 448 receiving yards. Klare is the most talented pass catcher in the Rams' tight end room; unfortunately, he will have to bide his time before making a fantasy impact.

38.name: Terrance Ferguson
38.comment: Ferguson did not get a ton of work his rookie year but did make some big plays with his chances. He caught just 11 passes but averaged 21.0 yards per reception and scored three touchdowns. Ferguson showed his big-play potential at the tight end spot. If he can have a solid offseason, Ferguson could move up the depth chart and play a bigger role in the Rams offense but he has a lot to compete with for playing time. Ferguson is a very fast tight end that can stretch the field. He is really good after the catch. Ferguson does need some work on his blocking but is a willing blocker that should continue to get better in that area with more seasoning.
38.outlook: You've heard of a crowded running back room, but rarely is the amount of talented tight ends a deterrent to fantasy football success. However, that's exactly the issue in Los Angeles. During the 2025 season, the Rams shifted toward using 13 personnel more often, meaning three tight ends could see the field at once, alongside Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Four tight ends - Tyler Higbee, Terrance Ferguson, Colby Parkinson, and Davis Allen - were part of the rotation, to varying degrees. Ferguson only played 38% of the team's offensive snaps. The Rams' brass complicated matters even more by drafting Max Klare in the second round of the NFL Draft. Ferguson, a second-round pick in 2025, is the most explosive of the group. He led all tight ends in deep targets, despite earning 25 total all season. The receiving upside is tremendous, but the snap count may not be up to snuff.

39.name: Darnell Washington
39.comment: Washington was third on the depth chart for the Steelers last year but still got plenty of playing time because the team used a lot of multiple tight end sets. He had career highs in receptions (31) and yards (364). He had more than 50 yards just two games, though, and reached double-digit fantasy points just once. Washington is likely to be the top backup for the Steelers this year. Washington is a physical specimen that can be a very tough cover for the tight end position. Washington can make the spectacular catch and is a top athlete at the position. He remains a little raw, though, and can lack consistency because of that.
39.outlook: Washington could have a few big games but will be inconsistent in a backup role, getting limited work. As long as Pat Freiermuth is healthy, Washington will get sporadic work. He might get 30 catches for 350 yards and a couple scores.

40.name: Tyler Higbee
40.comment: HIgbee was limited to 10 games last season because of injury. He had three games with double-digit fantasy points. Higbee had 25 receptions for 281 yards and three touchdowns. He has failed to top 50 receptions three straight seasons. Higbee will continue to be a part of the Rams passing game but could lose out on a little more playing time to younger options this year. He is 33 years old and his numbers are trending down. Higbee is a good route runner with plus hands. He does well on shorter routes, moving the chains. His blocking has improved through the years, making him more of an asset in the running game.
40.outlook: Higbee isn't a surefire fantasy starter anymore but likely worth a spot start or two along the way. He is capable of the big game in this offense. He can get around 30 receptions for 300 yards and three touchdowns.

41.name: Colby Parkinson
41.comment: Parkinson had his best season as a pro in year two with the Rams. He was 16th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. Parkinson had 43 receptions for 408 yards and eight touchdowns. He was a top red-zone threat for the Rams. Parkinson did get more playing time because of injury, though. He might have a hard time getting as much work, especially if Terrance Ferguson becomes a bigger part of the Rams offense. Parkinson has 25 or more receptions four straight seasons. Parkinson is a very tall tight end that can make the tough catch in traffic. He is great at getting the ball at it's highest point. Parkinson also is very athletic for a man of his size. He does lack some speed, though, and does little after the catch.
41.outlook: Parkinson has some red-zone potential and could get some receptions in this offense. He has a lot to compete with for playing time and targets, though, so he is a risk to take for fantasy teams. He might get around 30 receptions for 300 yards and four touchdowns.

42.name: Ja'Tavion Sanders
42.comment: Sanders did not do much better in year two and was hurt late in the season, missing the last four games because of a ankle injury. He had 29 receptions for 190 yards and a touchdown before getting hurt. Sanders had just a game all season reaching double-digit fantasy points, which was in Week 2. Sanders is likely stuck as the No. 2 tight end in Carolina. He has posted similar numbers each of his first two seasons. Sanders is more of a pass-catching tight end. He is a willing blocker but needs to improve in that area if he hopes to get even more playing time going forward. Sanders can stretch the field in a hurry because of his speed and is a good athlete for the position.
42.outlook: Sanders has done little to date and a sudden breakout seems unlikely. He might improve a little on last year but don't expect a huge jump. He might get 35 receptions for 350 yards and a score or two.

43.name: Dawson Knox
43.comment: Knox was hit or miss sharing time with Dalton Kincaid last year for the Bills once again. He hd 36 receptions for 417 yards and four touchdowns. He had a few more big games than the last few seasons, though, topping double-digit fantasy points three times. Knox had two straight seasons with 22 receptions before last year. Expect him to play behind Kincaid once again this season. Knox is a good route runner that can make plays down the field. He has plus hands and does well as a blocker. He can be an asset to the running game as well as a solid red-zone target.
43.outlook: Knox had a few big games last year and that might be the case again this year but it will be hard to predict when they might come. He will be risky to use for fantasy teams. Knox might get around 25 receptions for 300 yards and a few scores.

44.name: Greg Dulcich
44.comment: Dulcich emerged as a dependable target in the Dolphins passing game last year, catching 26 passes for 335 yards and a touchdown the last 10 games of the season. He had his best game Week 17, finishing with five receptions for 58 yards and a touchdown. This was his best season since his rookie year. Dulcich might have earned a role with the team for the coming season with his solid play down the stretch. He could be the top pass-catching tight end for Miami this season. Dulcich is a solid pass catcher with plus hands. He runs good routes and can be a tough cover down the seam. Dulcich is not much of a blocker, which can impact his playing time.
44.outlook: Dulcich has been a huge disappointment to date but last year gives you a little hope. But even if he ends up starting for Miami, his numbers won't be anything too special. He might be worth a late-round look in deeper formats. Look for around 30 receptions for 300 yards and a score or two.

45.name: Noah Fant
45.comment: Fant got plenty of work his first season in Cincinnati, catching 34 passes fro 288 yards and three touchdowns in a reserve role. He made some plays with his chances and proved to be a reliable backup tight end. He is expected to play a similar role this year with the Saints. Fant has at least 32 receptions every season in the NFL. Fant has a lot of ability but has lacked some consistency throughout his career. He can stretch the seam well because of his size and speed. He plays more like a receiver than a tight end. Fant also isn't a bad blocker.
45.outlook: Fant will be hit or miss once again in a backup role. He has posted similar numbers throughout his career recently, so don't expect a sudden huge spike in production. He is likely to get around 30 receptions for 300 yards and a few touchdowns, making him worth a look in deeper formats.

46.name: Nate Boerkircher
46.comment: Jacksonville picked Boerkircher in the second round of this year's draft. He didn't do a whole lot in college the Jaguars thought enough of him to take him in the second round. He caught just 19 passes his last season in college. He has decent speed and is a willing blocker. He has three-down ability with more seasoning. He should be second or third on the depth chart his rookie season, playing behind starter Brenton Strange.
46.outlook: Most thought Boerkircher was a big reach for the Jaguars in the draft. Even with that said, he could play a role his rookie year. Just don't expect big numbers. He might get 30 or so receptions for 300 yards and a few scores.

47.name: Cole Kmet
47.comment: Kmet became more of a backup last season because of Colston Loveland. Kmet had 30 receptions, his lowest total since his rookie year. Kmet had just a game all year reaching double-digit fantasy points. Kmet is expected to serve a similar backup role to Loveland this year. Kmet has at least 50 receptions three of six seasons. Kmet is a huge target at tight end. He has very good hands and good speed down the seam. He also is tough to bring down because of his size. He isn't much of a blocker, though, and doesn't have top speed for the position.
47.outlook: Kmet needs a change of scenery to be a big help to fantasy teams. His production is not going to be great in a backup role. He can get around 30 receptions for 300 yard and a few scores.

48.name: Michael Mayer
48.comment: Mayer played a backup role once again last year, playing behind the talented Brock Bowers. Mayer did have the most productive season of his career, though, catching 35 passes for 328 yards and a touchdown. He had a few big games along the way, having 16-plus fantasy points two games. But as long as Bowers is around, Mayer is not going to get a ton of weekly chances. Mayer has 20-plus receptions all three seasons in the NFL. Mayer is a very good blocker and reliable pass catcher. He isn't flashy but knows how to get open and move the chains. His route running needs some work, but should continue to get better with more seasoning.
48.outlook: Mayer would look a lot better if not for Bowers. But as long as Bowers is healthy and playing, Mayers is going to be limited. He might finish with similar numbers to last year, getting 30 receptions for 300 yards and a score or two.

49.name: Noah Gray
49.comment: Gray continues to backup Travis Kelce and do well in that role. He had 21 receptions last year and has topped 20 receptions four straight seasons. But as long as Kelce is around and healthy, Gray will get little playing time. Gray can be an asset in the passing game. He can runs good routes and does well in separating from defenders. He does lack some size for the position and won't make many plays after the catch.
49.outlook: Gray is worth a look in deeper formats. He might get a little more playing with Kelce another year older. But even with that said, look for around 30 receptions for 300 yards and a few scores.

50.name: Theo Johnson
50.comment: Johnson about doubled his stats from his rookie season, serving as the Giants starter from day one. He had 45 receptions for 528 yards and five touchdowns. Johnson was 18th overall in fantasy tight end scoring. He had seven games with double-digit fantasy points, showing good consistency. Unfortunately for Johnson, the Giants signed Isaiah Likely to a big contract this offseason to become their top tight end. This moves Johnson to a backup role going forward. Johnson has very good size. He does well on contested catches and is a solid route runner. He is a willing blocker but needs improvement in that area. He also doesn't do much after the catch.
50.outlook: Johnson would look a lot better if Likely were not around. But as long as Likely is healthy and playing, Johnson will have minimal fantasy value. He might get around 25 receptions for 300 yards and a few scores.

51.name: Austin Hooper
51.comment: Hooper saw a decrease in playing time his second season in New England. He took a backseat to starter Hunter Henry most weeks. Hooper had 21 receptions for 263 yards and two touchdowns after getting 45 receptions his previous season. Hooper failed to reach double-digit fantasy points any game. He signed with the Falcons this offseason to take over their No. 2 tight end role. He started his career in Atlanta and had his best seasons as a pro with the team. Hooper has 40-plus receptions six of 10 seasons. Hooper can be a top target at tight end because of his athleticism and speed. He isn't much of a blocker, though, and drops can be an issue, but he has improved in that area in recent years. He is more of a complete tight end.
51.outlook: Hooper is likely to finish with similar numbers to last year, giving him little fantasy value. He won't get a ton of weekly work in a backup role. Hooper can get around 25 receptions for 250 yards and a couple scores.

52.name: Matthew Hibner
52.comment: The Ravens added some youth to their tight end room, picking Hibner in the fourth round. He has a chance to compete for the top backup role behind Mark Andrews his rookie season. Hibner is a good downfield threat at the position. He can make the tough catch and plays after the catch. Hibner also is a solid blocker, showing promise in that area. He could become the future starter at the position for the Ravens.
52.outlook: Hibner doesn't have a ton of value his rookie season. He might struggle to find the field consistently. Look for around 20 receptions for 250 yards and a few scores.

53.name: Charlie Kolar
53.comment: Kolar was third on the depth chart late year for the Ravens once again but set a career-high with 10 receptions for 142 yards and two touchdowns. He made a few plays with his chances in the passing game. Kolar got most of his playing time because of his big-time blocking ability. He is one of the top blocking tight ends in football. Kolar signed a pretty big deal with the Chargers after the season. He might get a few more chances in the passing game with his new team but still will get most of his playing time to block. Kolar has good size and strength. He makes the tough catch and runs pretty good routes.
53.outlook: Kolar might see an uptick in targets but probably not enough to help fantasy teams. He will not be the top pass-catching tight end on the roster. He could get 20 receptions for 250 yards and a few scores.

54.name: Josh Oliver
54.comment: Oliver got a few more starts last year because of injury but still didn't do much in a Vikings offense that struggled throwing the ball. Oliver had 15 receptions for 160 yards and four touchdowns. His big positive was his work in the red zone. He has posted similar numbers in three seasons with Minnesota, averaging 20 receptions for 210 yards and three touchdowns per season. He will continue to play a backup role this coming year. Oliver does his best work as a blocker, which will get him on the field. He is a good athlete with a knack for making the big play. He is a very tough cover because of his size and athleticism. He lacks consistency, though, and will drop some passes. He is a very good blocker, which is his biggest asset to an offense.
54.outlook: Oliver might have a big game or two but also will disappear most weeks. He'll be very hit or miss, getting most of his work as a blocker. He could get around 20 catches for 200 yards and a couple scores.

55.name: Marlin Klein
55.comment: Klein was a second-round pick by the Texans in this year's draft. He should serve a backup role to Dalton Schultz his rookie year, learning behind the veteran tight end. Klein is a developmental tight end that the Texans hope develops into their starter in a season or two. Klein has three-down potential at the position, already doing a good job as a blocker.
