He probably needs a little more work catching the ball more than anything. He has good speed to get by defenders and can make the big play in the passing game. He is not a great route runner, though.
55.outlook: Klein might get a little work his rookie year but don't expect a ton in his current role. He might get 20 receptions for 250 yards and a few scores. His fantasy value is more down the road.

56.name: Daniel Bellinger
56.comment: Bellinger played sparingly once again last year for the Giants, catching 19 passes for 286 yards and two touchdowns. He has failed to top 20 receptions two straight seasons. Bellinger heads to the Titans and will likely be the top backup for his new team, reuniting with his old coach, Brian Daboll. Bellinger is a pretty good two-way tight end. He catches the ball well and has good size for the position. Bellinger is a solid route runner and a willing blocker.
56.outlook: Bellinger has little fantasy value - even with a move to a new team. He just won't get a ton of work in the passing game. He might get around 20 receptions for 200 yards.

57.name: Eli Raridon
57.comment: New England selected Raridon in the third round of this year's draft. He has a chance to be the top backup to veteran Hunter Henry in his rookie season. Raridon didn't produce great numbers in college but tested great at the combine. He has the ability to help as both a pass catcher and blocker. He has plus hands and can make plays after the catch. Raridon does need to shore up his route running some at the next level and he will drop some passes.
57.outlook: Raridon could have a big game or two in this passing game but will be really hit or miss in a reserve role. He is going to look a lot better once Henry moves on. Until then, his fantasy value is limited.

58.name: Tommy Tremble
58.comment: Tremble posted similar numbers to the rest of his career last season, catching 27 passes for 249 yards and two touchdowns. He did set a career-high in receptions but still failed to top 30 catches. His numbers have been eerily close throughout his five-year career. Tremble should continue to get some weekly chances to catch the ball but serve more of a reserve role. Tremble catches the ball well on underneath routes and can make plays after the catch. He is a good blocker for the position.
58.outlook: Tremble does not have a lot of fantasy value in his current role. Unless he starts to get more weekly targets, he probably isn't worth a roster spot. He might get 25 receptions for 250 yards and a few scores.

59.name: Adam Trautman
59.comment: Trautman had 20 receptions for 195 yards and a touchdown for the Broncos last year. He has played a similar reserve role the last three years in Denver. Trautman has averaged 18 receptions for 196 yards and two touchdowns per season for the Broncos. He is expected to play a similar reserve role this coming year. Trautman is a very athletic player. He is a tall tight end that can be explosive after the catch. His route running is just alright and he will drop some passes.
59.outlook: Trautman has done little to date. Don't expect a sudden turnaround. He is not a very exciting fantasy option - even when getting a chance to start. He might get around 20 catches for 200 yards and a score.

60.name: Elijah Higgins
60.comment: Higgins was the top backup for the Cardinals once again last year and had his best season to date, finishing with 30 receptions for 301 yards. He had one game all year reaching double-digit fantasy points. He played a backseat to Trey McBride once again but got some weekly chances to catch the ball in a backup role. Higgins had 20 or more receptions two straight years. Higgins should be behind McBride on the Cardinals depth chart once again this year. Higgins does well on the contested catch and uses his size to his advantage. He also does well in making plays after the catch, especially if you consider his size.
60.outlook: Higgins is more of a handcuff to McBride than anything. He will have a hard time posting big games in a backup role. Look for around 20 receptions for 200 yard and a score or two.

61.name: Mitchell Evans
61.comment: Evans played a backup role his rookie season and finished with 19 receptions for 171 yards and two touchdowns. He is likely in a backup role again this coming year. Evans is a two-way player at the position, helping as a receiver and blocker. He has solid hands and gets the most out of his ability. He knows how to get open and move the chains. He lacks some explosiveness and is just a so-so athlete.
61.outlook: Evans might get a few weekly chances but don't expect much of an impact at this stage of his career. He could get around 20 receptions for 200 yards.

62.name: Foster Moreau
62.comment: Moreau had an ankle injury that kept him out of some action last year, causing him to finish with his worst numbers in several seasons. He had seven catches for 59 yards in 11 games. He had at least 21 receptions four straight seasons before last year. He signed with the Texans this offseason to serve as a depth player for his new team. Moreau is a good blocking tight end that helps him get on the field. He has some skills as a receiver, though. He can make plays after the catch and run by defenders down the seam. He lacks a little athleticism, though.
62.outlook: Moreau is not going to see a sudden uptick in production with his new team. His ceiling is limited. He might get 20 receptions for 200 yards and a score or two.

63.name: Luke Musgrave
63.comment: Musgrave started about half the season last year because of an injury to Tucker Kraft, but didn't exactly take advantage of that opportunity. He did not reach double-digit fantasy points in a single game. He had 24 receptions for 252 yards. Musgrave has 20-plus receptions two of three seasons. He is stuck in a backup role for the Packers, playing behind the talented Kraft. Musgrave is a big target and solid route runner at the position. He knows how to get open and can use his size and athleticism to make the big play. He can be a little injury prone, missing games two of his first three seasons.
63.outlook: Musgrave is not much of a fantasy option. He showed last year that even if he gets to start he won't be much help to fantasy teams. He just won't get enough consistent work. Musgrave might get 25 receptions for 250 yards.

64.name: Grant Calcaterra
64.comment: Calcaterra was third on the Eagles depth chart most of last year and had just nine receptions for 76 yards and a touchdown. His numbers were down from the previous season when he had a career-best 24 receptions. Calcaterra has fewer than double-digit receptions three of four seasons. He re-signed with the Eagles after the season and will look to earn the top backup role behind Dallas Goedert. Calcaterra is a good receiving tight end that runs good routes and can make the contested catch. He is not much of a blocker and will struggle some in press coverage.
64.outlook: Calcaterra will have minimal fantasy value even if he is the top backup this season. He might get 20 receptions for 200 yards and a touchdown.

65.name: Brock Wright
65.comment: Wright had a neck injury cut his season short but he wasn't doing much for fantasy teams even before getting hurt. He had 14 receptions for 108 yards and two touchdowns in 11 games. Wright has 70 receptions for his career but has found the end zone 11 times. He serves the backup role well and should continue to have that job. Wright will find the field because of his blocking ability. He doesn't have a ton of experience catching the ball but is getting better in that area and can be an asset in the red zone.
65.outlook: Wright is not a very exciting fantasy option. He has a little touchdown potential but it will be hard to figure out when those might come. Look for around 20 catches for 200 yards and a few scores.

66.name: Jackson Hawes
66.comment: Hawes was the No. 3 tight end for the Bills his rookie season. He got some work in that role, catching 16 passes for 187 yards and three touchdowns. He is likely stuck in a similar role this year with two solid tight ends ahead of him on depth chart. Hawes is a good blocking tight end, getting most of is playing time because of that. He is not much of a pass catcher but made some plays with his past chances.
66.outlook: Hawes is a plus for the Bills running game, but that won't help fantasy teams when it comes to his fantasy production. He won't get a ton of work in that area.

67.name: Davis Allen
67.comment: Allen got a little more work last year for the Rams. They use plenty of two tight ends sets, getting Allen on the field. He had 24 receptions for 208 yards and three touchdowns. Last season was the first time in his three-year career that Allen managed more than 10 receptions. He should be third or fourth on the depth chart once again this year for the Rams. Allen does well at making the contested catch and can really get up to catch a ball. He is a good athlete for the tight end position. He isn't much of a blocker and his route running can be a little sloppy.
67.outlook: Allen could get on the field a little but not enough to help most fantasy teams. He could be worth adding if injury hits, though. He might get around 20 catches for 200 yards and a score or two.

68.name: Brevin Jordan
68.comment: Jordan missed all of last season after tearing his ACL before the start of the season. Jordan has suffered knee injuries each of the last two seasons, so nothing is certain for him going forward. He could play a depth role if healthy for the coming season. Jordan has never topped 20 receptions in a season. Jordan does well after the catch and can do well on shorter routes. He does lack a little top-end speed, though, and could use some work blocking. Jordan still has some room to grow but hasn't done a whole lot with his chances to date.
68.outlook: Jordan is a huge injury risk. Plus, he has never done much in the past. He just isn't worth the risk. Jordan might get 20 receptions for 200 yards.

69.name: Ben Sinnott
69.comment: Sinnott did not take much of a step forward in year two. He had 11 receptions for 114 yards and a touchdown, giving him 16 receptions in two seasons. Sinnott seems stuck at second or third on the Commanders depth chart after the team signed Chig Okonkwo to be their starting tight end. Sinnott just hasn't progressed as expected. Sinnott is a solid pass catching tight end that does well after the catch. He runs solid routes and is a top athlete for the position. He isn't much of a blocker, though, and will need to continue to improve in that area if he hopes to be on the field a lot more often.
69.outlook: Sinnott isn't worth a draft pick at this stage of his career. He will have a hard time getting much consistent work in his current role. Sinnott can get around 20 receptions for 200 yards.

70.name: Cade Stover
70.comment: Stover did not get much more work in year two, playing behind Dalton Schultz once again. Stover also had some injury issues, limiting him to nine games. He had 12 receptions after having 15 his rookie year. He should continue to take a backseat to Schultz in the Texans offense, serving as the No. 2 or 3 tight end. Stover is a very good athlete that is still learning the position after starting his college career as a defensive player. Stover needs to shore up his route running but continues to make strides in that area. He catches the ball well and uses his athleticism to his advantage. Stover also is a willing blocker that is not a liability in that area.
70.outlook: Stover might look better in a few seasons but won't be much of a help to fantasy teams right now unless injury hits. He could get 20 receptions for 200 yards.

71.name: Jeremy Ruckert
71.comment: Ruckert set more career highs last year, catching 23 passes for 179 yards and a touchdown. He has at least 16 receptions three straight seasons. Ruckert gets most of his playing time because of his blocking ability, though. He should continue to play a reserve role for the Jets and get playing time as the top blocking tight end for the team. Ruckert lacks a little speed and is just a so-so route runner. He can be a punishing blocker, though.
71.outlook: Ruckert is a big stretch for fantasy teams. He just won't get a lot of work in the passing game. Look for around 20 receptions for 200 yards. And he has just a touchdown in four seasons.

72.name: Taysom Hill
72.comment: Hill had some injury issues once again but wasn't used nearly as much with a new coaching staff in place. He had 205 total yards and a touchdown in 13 games. He also was 2-of-6 for 57 yards and a touchdown throwing the ball. Hill got most of his work running the ball, rushing 52 times for 114 yards. Hill is 35 years old and coming off maybe the worst season of his career, so nothing is certain about his future right now. It is up in the air. Hill has 550-plus total yards three of six seasons. When healthy, Hill plays a variety of roles offensively. Hill has good speed and is a load to bring down in the open field because of his size and strength. Hill isn't much of a thrower, lacking some accuracy and touch, especially on deeper throws. Hill is a much improved pass catcher and can be a load to bring down as a running back because of his size. He does well in goal-line situations, giving him touchdown potential.
72.outlook: Hill was a bust last year and a turnaround this year seems a stretch. Go with other younger, more exciting options come draft day. His best days are behind him.

73.name: Tanner Hudson
73.comment: Hudson had 19 receptions for the second straight season with the Bengals, playing a backup role with the team. Hudson serves the backup role well. He has double-digit receptions four straight seasons. He even has a season with 39 receptions. Hudson is expected to serve a similar backup role this year. Hudson can move the chains and help as a blocker. Hudson has pretty good hands and runs decent routes. He has just four drops for his career.
73.outlook: Hudson will be hard pressed to hep fantasy teams in his current role. He could get 20 receptions for 200 yards and a touchdown.

74.name: Will Dissly
74.comment: Dissly had just 11 receptions last year after getting a career-best 50 his previous season. He did not get near the work in his second season for the Chargers. Dissly's season high in yards was just 28. Dissly should continue to play a reserve role this coming year, a role he can serve well. Dissly has 20-plus receptions five of seven seasons. Dissly is a big tight end but runs solid routes and has a knack for making the big play. He also does well in the red zone because of his size and strength. And he blocks pretty well, giving him a chance to find the field more often.
74.outlook: Dissly is not really draft material at this stage of his career. His numbers are trending the wrong way. He is a long shot to become fantasy relevant once again. He might get 20 catches for 200 yards.

75.name: Oscar Delp
75.comment: The Saints took Delp in the third round of this year's draft. Delp has good size for the position and is a willing blocker. He has shown some three-down potential but will need to add a little strength at the next level. Delp can stretch the field a little but does better on shorter routes. He runs decent routes and has a knack for getting open. He is likely third on the depth chart his rookie season New Orleans.
75.outlook: For fantasy managers, the importance of patience cannot be overstated when identifying which tight ends have an opportunity to produce and which are best left on the waiver wire. One such tight end that is of interest, even as a rookie, is Oscar Delp of the New Orleans Saints. While rookie tight ends historically aren't known for production early in their careers, Delp finds himself in an intriguing situation. While Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant likely see the bulk of the receiving work early on, Delp is a better blocker than either tight end. It is pretty good as a pass catcher in his own right, despite the college production never living up to the hype, in part due to erratic quarterback play at Georgia. As an athlete, Delp compares favourably to Brock Bowers: he is bigger and faster, and his athletic score of 89 is 7 points higher than Bowers'. There is a path for fantasy relevance for Delp in 2026. Delp has the tools, and Tyler Shough is a vast improvement at the quarterback position. If Delp can surpass Fant of the depth chart, he could find himself on the field lining up in-line, thus allowing himself to earn future opportunities. Delp may not be the answer in season-long fantasy leagues, but in best ball formats, he is worth a late-round flier.

76.name: Luke Schoonmaker
76.comment: Schoonmaker saw his playing time decrease a little last year, catching 14 passes for 132 yards. He failed to top 20 receptions like he did the previous year. Schoonmaker has 49 receptions in three seasons. He should continue to be the top backup for the Cowboys, playing behind Jake Ferguson. Schoonmaker is a solid blocking tight end but also can help as a receiver. He runs plus routes for a tight end and has good hands. He will struggle a little with the contested catch and lacks a little strength.
76.outlook: Schoonmaker has little potential as long as Ferguson is around. He will struggle to get much work. He might get 20 receptions for 200 yards.

77.name: Seydou Traore
77.comment: Miami selected Traore in the fifth round of this year's draft. He is a good athlete that can stretch the field in a hurry because of his size and speed. He also is good at making plays after the catch. He does alright as a blocker but needs some work in that area. Traore should be third or fourth on the depth chart for the Dolphins his rookie year.
77.outlook: Traore is a litle intriguing if he starts getting consistent work but not sure that happens his rookie year. He is not draft material. He might get 15 receptions for 200 yards.

78.name: Drew Sample
78.comment: Sample had 15 receptions for 106 yards and a touchdown in a reserve role once again for the Bengals. He has at least 15 catches three straight seasons with Cincinnati. He has just one season in his seven-year career with more than 170 yards. Sample gets most of his playing time because of his ability to block. Sample is a solid blocker that is capable of making some big plays down the field. He also has good hands. He lacks some consistency, though, and isn't much of a route runner.
78.outlook: Sample isn't a great option even if he gets more playing time. He proved that when he played a lot six years back. He should help more as a blocker than a receiver. Sample can get 20 receptions for 150 yards and a score.

79.name: Mo Alie-Cox
79.comment: Alie-Cox had 13 receptions for 117 yards and a touchdown last season. His numbers have been very similar throughout his career, especially the last four seasons. Alie-Cox is more help as a blocker than anything and should continue to play a similar role this year. He will get the occasional look in the passing game. Alie-Cox has 20-plus receptions two of eight seasons. Alie-Cox is a very good athlete with good speed and leaping ability. He still isn't a very good route runner but is one of the premier blocking tight ends in the game.
79.outlook: Alie-Cox might have a good game or two, but it will be tough to predict when that will happen. He is a big stretch for fantasy teams. He might get 15 receptions for 200 yards and a touchdown.

80.name: Sam Roush
80.comment: The Bears picked Roush in the third round of this year's draft. He joins a crowded tight end room that already has Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet. Roush could struggle to carve out much of a role his rookie season. Roush is probably a better blocker than receiver at this stage of his career. His blocking ability might get him on the field some as the third tight end for the Bears. He will catch some passes, though, and does well on the shorter routes.
80.outlook: Roush is not in a good fantasy situation. He will struggled to get many targets in this offense unless injury hits at tight end.

81.name: Donald Parham
81.comment: Parham missed all of last year, suffering a torn Achilles' before the start of the season. He did not play at all and has a long road back from the serious injury. If he can get healthy, Parham will look to earn a depth role. Parham has 67 receptions for his career and two years with 20 or more receptions. Parham has some talent but hasn't been consistent when on the field. He isn't much of a blocker but can play like a receiver more than a tight end. He is a good combination of size and speed, making him a tough cover.
81.outlook: Parham might have a big game or two if he makes a roster, but is a tough player for fantasy teams to trust. He will be inconsistent. He could get around 15 receptions for 200 yards.

82.name: Justin Joly
82.comment: Denver selected Joly in the fifth round of this year's draft. He is expected to be third on the depth chart his rookie season. Joly might be the future of the position, though, and their starter in a few seasons. Joly is a pretty complete tight end. He is a willing blocker and does his best work as a pass catcher. He is good at getting open in a hurry and making some plays after the catch. Joly also has pretty strong hands, doing well on the contested catch.
82.outlook: After Evan Engram flopped with just 461 receiving yards in his first year as a member of the Denver Broncos, it was expected that the team would address the tight end position in April's NFL Draft. Following several trades, it wasn't until the fifth round that the team selected North Carolina State's Justin Joly. The 2026 NFL Draft featured a record number of tight ends selected (21), but many were blocking archetypes. Entering the event, Joly was on the shortlist of receiving specialists who could be fantasy-relevant in their first year after leading the Wolfpack in receptions (49) last season. He trailed only KC Concepcion with 43 catches in 2024. NC State's anemic passing offense over the last two seasons, which failed to produce a 3,500-yard passer, slowed Joly's production. Still, his hands, intermediate route running, and ability to separate for a shorter tight end ("6-foot-3") stand out on tape. In addition to having a potential $14.4-million cap savings if cut, Engram has missed nine games over the last two seasons, and Adam Trautman's career high in receptions (27) shows he's not a bona fide top receiving option at the position, either. Denver could badly use someone to step up, and it could be the rookie Joly, who is also battling seventh-rounder Dallen Bentley for snaps in this room. In redraft formats, Joly could start to enter "last-round flier" territory in deep leagues if Engram were cut during the preseason. However, until that confirmation, it's still tough to expect any immediate value from him in 2026, so he's a stash in dynasty leagues for now.

83.name: John Bates
83.comment: Bates had 11 receptions for 103 yards and a touchdown in a reserve role for the Commanders last year. Bates has just 19 receptions his last two seasons and never had more than 20 catches in a season. Bates is expected to play a similar reserver role this year. Bates catches the ball well and can make plays after the catch. He lacks consistency, though, and doesn't make a lot of plays after contact. He gets most of his playing time because of his blocking ability.
83.outlook: Bates is not a very exciting fantasy option. He might get a few more weekly targets this year but expect a lot of inconsistency. He could get 15 catches for 150 yards.

85.name: Kylen Granson
85.comment: Granson played every game his first season with the Eagles but didn't get much work in the passing game. He had seven receptions for 40 yards. It was his first season as a pro failing to reach double-digit receptions. He signed with the Titans this offseason and will serve a depth role with his new team. Granson is not too explosive at the position but does well on shorter routes and can make plays after the catch. He is just a so-so blocker and lacks some speed for the position. He won't make a ton of plays down the field.
85.outlook: Granson has done little in recent seasons. A move to Tennessee is not expected to get him much more work. He is not draft material. Granson can get around 15 receptions for 150 yards.

86.name: Stone Smartt
86.comment: Smartt played nearly every game last year with the Jets but didn't get any catches until Week 16. He had seven receptions for 52 yards on the season. Smartt has double-digit receptions two of his last three seasons but never had more than 20 catches in a year. Smartt will look to earn a backup role for the coming season. Smartt has good size for the position and does well after the catch for a tight end. He is strong on seam routes. He lacks a little polish, though, and won't be a huge asset as a blocker.
86.outlook: Smartt might get some chances but don't expect anything huge in his current role. Look for around 15 receptions.

87.name: Tyler Conklin
87.comment: Conklin had seven receptions for 101 yards in 13 games for the Chargers last year. He saw a big downturn in production after four straight seasons with 50-plus receptions. He heads to the Lions this year and is likely third on their depth chart at tight end. He could get similar playing time to last year. Conklin can be a reliable target in the passing game. He is a decent blocker and athlete. He catches the ball well, especially in traffic. He lacks some top speed, though, which can limit his big-play ability.
87.outlook: Conklin was a bust last year, failing to earn a big role with his new team. It could be more of the same this year in Detroit. He might get 10 catches for 100 yards.

88.name: Bauer Sharp
88.comment: The Bucs took Sharp in the sixth round of this year's draft. He looks the part of an NFL tight end, having good size and speed. He is a willing blocker but needs some improvement in that area. Sharp is a quick tight end that runs pretty good routes. He catches the ball pretty well and jumps well for a man of his size. He should be third or fourth on the depth chart his rookie season for the Bucs.
88.outlook: Sharp could play his way into a larger role for the Bucs with the team having little behind Cade Otton. But he still seems a long shot to make a fantasy impact as a rookie.

89.name: James Mitchell
89.comment: Mitchell played five games his first season with the Panthers, catching three passes for 28 yards. He played a deep reserve role with the team, getting little playing time. He has 16 receptions in four NFL seasons. Mitchell re-signed with the Panthers after the season and will likely play a similar reserve role this coming year. Mitchell is an athletic tight end that can make plays down the seam or after the catch. He is just a so-so run blocker and could use some work on his route running.
89.outlook: Mitchell is not a very exciting fantasy option. He will have a hard time finding the field consistently.

90.name: Jelani Woods
90.comment: Woods was picked up by the Jets before last season and got in four games, catching a pass for four yards. He has battled injury issues throughout his career and done little since his rookie season, a year he had 25 receptions for 312 yards. The Jets re-signed him after the season and he'll compete for a depth role with his new team. Woods is a good athlete with good size and strength. He is an improved blocker and receiver. Woods can be very tough after the catch because of his size and speed. He remains a bit raw since he has played little since entering the league, so inconsistency can be a problem. And injuries are a major concern after the last few seasons.
90.outlook: Woods might be worth a spot play if he is getting consistent playing time. He might have a few big games along the way but needs to earn that role in the offense first. He could get around 10 receptions for 125 yards.

91.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
91.comment: Spann-Ford played sparingly again last year in a deep reserve role for the Cowboys. He had nine receptions for the second straight season, giving him 18 catches in two years. He should have a similar role this coming season, having two pretty good tight ends ahead of him right now.
91.outlook: Spann-Ford is going to have a hard time getting much consistent work. He will be lucky to reach double-digit receptions.

92.name: Josh Whyle
92.comment: Whyle had five receptions for 36 yards and a touchdown in his first season with the Packers. He played a deep reserve role, getting in eight games. He has failed to reach double-digit receptions two of three seasons. Whyle is likely to play another deep reserve role this year. Whyle is a good athlete that does well on the jump ball. He also is a wiling blocker that does well on the move. He does lack a little strength and will struggle some on the contested catch.
92.outlook: Whyle is likely to finish with similar numbers to last year, making him a big stretch for fantasy teams. He could get 10 receptions for 100 yards and a score.

93.name: Connor Heyward
93.comment: Heyward got more chances to run the ball last year, getting a chance to play a lot of fullback. He ran 15 times for 43 yards and two touchdowns. He had just three receptions, which was a career low for him. Heyward has two straight seasons failing to reach double-digit catches. He signed with the Raiders this offseason and likely is to serve more of a fullback role this season with his new team. Heyward is a good pass catcher and solid blocker. He will do better on shorter passes but is not going to make a lot of big plays down the field. His plus hands help make up for some other downfalls. He also is a good short-yardage option running the ball, converting on a lot of those attempts last year.
93.outlook: Heyward gets a little work in the passing game and some occasional carries but not enough consistent touches to help fantasy teams. He could see his numbers improve some this year with a new team but don't expect a big leap. He could get around 200 total yards and a few scores.

94.name: Erick All
94.comment: All missed all of his rookie seasons because of a torn ACL and needed a second surgery on the injury before the start of last year, causing him to miss all of his second season as well. At this point, his career might be in jeopardy. When healthy, All could be the future for the Bengals at the position. All is a good athlete that does well at stretching the field down the seam. He also is a pretty good pass catcher and can do well after the catch. He isn't a very physical tight end, though, and injuries are a big concern going forward.
94.outlook: All is a wait and see player. He might be worth grabbing if he proves to be healthy and starts to get some playing time. Until that happens, don't bother.

95.name: Durham Smythe
95.comment: Smythe played every game his first season with the Bears, catching four passes for 25 yards. He served as the to blocking tight end for the Bears much of the season. He heads to the Ravens this year to likely serve a similar role. He has fewer than double-digit receptions two straight seasons but does have two seasons with 30-plus receptions, producing some decent numbers in the passing game when given the chance. Smythe should find the field because of his top blocking ability, though. Smythe will make some plays catching the ball when given a chance, but his best chance for playing time comes as a blocking tight end.
95.outlook: Smythe is a big stretch for fantasy teams. He won't get many chances to catch the ball, possibly getting 10 catches for 100 yards.

96.name: Lucas Krull
96.comment: Krull missed most of last year because of a foot injury. He had two receptions for 15 yards in three games. He re-signed with the Broncos after the season and will look to play a depth role at tight end. Krull has 29 receptions in three seasons with Denver.
96.outlook: Krull is a long shot to start producing enough to help fantasy teams. Go with much safer options.

97.name: Luke Farrell
97.comment: Farrell had 11 receptions for 85 yards and two touchdowns his first season with the 49ers. His numbers were really similar to his past two seasons with the Jaguars. Farrell should continue to serve a depth role for the coming season. He has 47 receptions in five seasons and never had more than 15 catches in a year. Farrell finds the field mostly because of his blocking ability. It could be more of the same for him this year. Farrell will continue to help as a blocker and get few targets on a weekly basis.
97.outlook: Farrell will help blocking more than receiving, limiting his fantasy value. He might get 10 catches for 100 yards.

98.name: Tanner Koziol
98.comment: Koziol was the second tight end picked by the Jaguars in this year's drat, getting selected in the fifth round. He is likely to play a deep reserve role his rookie season. Koziol has really good size for the position to help as a receiver and blocker. He is not much of a route runner and his blocking needs some work, but the potential is there for him. He could develop with a few years of seasoning under his belt.
98.outlook: Koziol is another developmental rookie. He is going to get little work as a rookie. He might be a fantasy factor in a few seasons if he makes some progress.

99.name: Julian Hill
99.comment: Hill had career-best numbers last year for the Dolphins, catching 15 passes for 140 yards. He has double-digit receptions two straight seasons. He signed with the Patriots after the season to serve a depth role with his new team. His biggest asset comes as a blocker, getting him on the field because of his ability in that area.
99.outlook: Hill is not going to help fantasy teams in his current role. He will help the running game more than the passing game. He might get 10 receptions.

100.name: Nate Adkins
100.comment: Adkins played a deep reserve role once again last year for the Broncos. He had six receptions for 48 yards and a touchdown. He has 24 receptions in three seasons. Adkins should play a similar reserve for the Broncos this season. He has a lot to compete with for targets at tight end.
100.outlook: Adkins is going to have a hard time getting much work. He might finish with similar numbers to his first three seasons in Denver.
